WITH rental_totals AS (
  SELECT i.store_id, p.rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY i.store_id, p.rental_id
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM rental_totals
)
SELECT rt.store_id,
       SUM(rt.total) AS total_payment_sum,
       AVG(rt.total - o.avg_total) AS avg_excess
FROM rental_totals rt
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE rt.total > o.avg_total
GROUP BY rt.store_id
ORDER BY rt.store_id

WITH rental_totals AS (
  SELECT i.store_id, p.rental_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY i.store_id, p.rental_id
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM rental_totals
)
SELECT rt.store_id,
       SUM(rt.total) AS total_payment_sum,
       AVG(rt.total - o.avg_total) AS avg_excess
FROM rental_totals rt
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE rt.total > o.avg_total
GROUP BY rt.store_id
ORDER BY rt.store_id

assumptions.assumption: The store of a rental is the store_id of the inventory copy rented (rental -> inventory); each rental maps to exactly one store, so grouping by store and rental_id is the same as grouping by rental.
The overall average is the mean of per-rental payment totals over all rentals that have at least one payment (rentals with no payments are not included as zero).

responses.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT p.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.rental_id, i.store_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS overall_avg FROM rental_totals) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.total_amount) AS total_payment_sum, AVG(rt.total_amount - o.overall_avg) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM rental_totals rt CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE rt.total_amount > o.overall_avg GROUP BY rt.store_id

assumptions.assumption: The overall average is taken over rentals that have at least one linked payment (rental totals computed from payments with non-null rental_id), across both stores together. Rentals with no payments are not counted as zero-total rentals.

responses.sql: WITH rental_totals AS (SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS total_amount FROM payment p JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id WHERE p.rental_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS overall_avg FROM rental_totals) SELECT rt.store_id, SUM(rt.total_amount) AS sum_of_rental_totals, AVG(rt.total_amount - o.overall_avg) AS avg_excess_over_overall_avg FROM rental_totals rt CROSS JOIN overall o WHERE rt.total_amount > o.overall_avg GROUP BY rt.store_id ORDER BY rt.store_id

assumptions.assumption: The overall average is taken over rentals that have at least one linked payment, since only those have a payment total, and it is computed across both stores combined.
The store comes from inventory.store_id via rental.inventory_id, not from the customer or staff.
